brief.t: A private bank promoted by the Hinduja Group, started in 1994; about 3,136 branches and banking outlets (March 2026).
In 2025, accounting lapses in its derivatives book (about ₹1,979 crore) led CEO Sumant Kathpalia to resign.
Rajiv Anand, former Deputy MD of Axis Bank, has been MD & CEO since 25 Aug 2025; ex-SBI MD Arijit Basu became Chairman on 31 Jan 2026.
FY 2025-26 standalone profit fell 64.7% to ₹933 crore as the bank cleaned up its books.
Recovery under way: Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit was ₹1,242 crore against a loss a year earlier, and Gross NPA fell to 2.73%.

timeline.t: IndusInd Bank started; inaugurated by then Finance Minister Dr Manmohan Singh.
Bought Deutsche Bank's credit card business in India.
Microfinance lender Bharat Financial Inclusion merged into the bank.
Derivative accounting lapses came to light; CEO resigned; Rajiv Anand took over in Aug 2025.

model.how: IndusInd earns mainly from the interest gap between loans and deposits. It is known for vehicle loans, microfinance (through Bharat Financial) and corporate banking, plus fees from cards and other products.
flow: Bank lends: vehicle, microfinance, business and personal loans

points: RBI must approve a private bank's CEO and Chairman; both changed at IndusInd in 2025–26.
Strong governance and accurate accounting are now a big theme for all banks after IndusInd's 2025 lapse.
It competes with larger private banks such as HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank.

numbers.say: IndusInd Bank is back in profit, earning ₹1,242 crore last quarter after a difficult 2025, under new CEO Rajiv Anand.

rivals.note: FY26 profit was low because of the 2025 clean-up; compare the recovery in recent quarters too.

network.local: IndusInd has a wide branch and vehicle-finance presence across North India, and its microfinance arm works deep in rural areas.

csr.t: IndusInd's CSR focuses on rural development, the environment, education and employability, inclusive sports and livelihoods.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Derivatives: Financial contracts (such as currency swaps) whose value depends on another asset. Wrong accounting of these caused IndusInd's 2025 problem.
glossary.Governance: The rules, controls and oversight that make sure a company is run honestly and correctly.
glossary.Microfinance: Small loans, often to women's groups in villages, without collateral.

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: What went wrong at IndusInd Bank in 2025?
Finance.a: Accounting lapses in its derivatives book, about ₹1,979 cr, were found. It cut profit and led to the CEO's resignation.

Finance.q: Why does strong internal control matter for a bank?
Finance.a: Banks hold public money; wrong numbers hurt trust, share price and depositors. Controls catch errors early.

Finance.q: Profit is back but FY26 fell 64.7%. How do you read that?
Finance.a: FY26 absorbed the clean-up costs; Q2 FY27 profit of ₹1,242 cr shows recovery, but asset quality must keep improving.

Marketing.q: How would you rebuild customer trust in IndusInd Bank?
Marketing.a: Transparent communication, strong service, visible new leadership and simple, honest product messaging.

Marketing.q: How would you market vehicle loans in a small town?
Marketing.a: Tie-ups with local dealers, quick approvals, regional-language campaigns and loan melas.

HR.q: How would you keep employees motivated after a leadership crisis?
HR.a: Clear communication from leaders, stable goals, recognition and a strong focus on ethics and training.

Sales.q: A customer is worried about IndusInd's 2025 news. What do you say?
Sales.a: Acknowledge it honestly; explain RBI regulation, deposit insurance basics, the new management and the return to profit.

Operations.q: How would you strengthen controls in a bank's treasury operations?
Operations.a: Independent checks, daily reconciliations, automated alerts and regular audits.

Other.q: What do you know about IndusInd Bank?
Other.a: A Hinduja-promoted private bank started in 1994, led by MD & CEO Rajiv Anand, back to profit in FY27 after a 2025 accounting lapse.

interview.why_us: IndusInd Bank is in a turnaround: after a hard 2025, it returned to profit with ₹1,242 crore last quarter under a new CEO and Chairman, and it is investing in new areas like banking for global capability centres. Joining during a rebuild means learning fast and seeing real change. I want to contribute to [your role] as the bank grows stronger.
ask: What are the leadership's top priorities for the next two years?
How has the bank strengthened its controls since 2025?
What does success look like for a new joiner in the first six months?

gd.t: Should bank CEOs be held personally responsible for accounting lapses?
gd.for: Leaders set the culture and controls.
gd.against: Lapses can happen deep in a team; systems and auditors also share blame.

gd.t: Can a bank fully recover trust after a scandal?
gd.for: IndusInd returned to profit within about a year.
gd.against: Trust is slow to rebuild; customers and investors stay cautious.

avoid: Don't name Sumant Kathpalia as CEO; he resigned in 2025. Rajiv Anand leads now.
Don't call IndusInd a public sector bank; it is private, promoted by the Hinduja Group.
Don't speak negatively about the bank's past; show you understand the recovery.
